about: Sniff's marking rule, written by hand (not generated). spot: right letter, right spot (a filled paw). near: in the answer, elsewhere (an outlined paw). none: not in the answer, or already used up (plain). Right spots are marked first; then, left to right, a letter is near only while the answer still has an unmarked copy of it.

vectors.name: every letter elsewhere but the last
the guess has n three times, the answer once at the fourth spot: that one is a spot, the earlier two are plain even though they come first
the guess has t three times, the answer once: the first is near, the rest plain
the guess has t twice, the answer twice: one spot, the other near
the guess has e three times, the answer twice, none in place: the first two near, the third plain
the answer has e twice, the guess once: near
both have e twice, both in place
both have o twice: one in place, the other elsewhere; every other letter elsewhere
p in place and again later: the later copy is plain, the answer has one p
